comment: The vectors pinning Prima.HostAPI as it crosses HTTP (Prima.WorkerWire): every call a runner makes and the report a worker service makes, sealed and signed with the keys of tests/fixtures/worker_auth.json, whose values keys repeats (root_hex is the root every other key derives from). Every consumer reproduces each call from its fields: body is the request body Prima.WorkerWire.request_body/2 writes, sealed as body_sealed in the body direction under the attempt seal key with body_iv_hex (Prima.WorkerAuth.seal_call/5); header is the host-call header over body_sealed, the bytes posted, under the attempt call key; answer is the answer written for it, sealed as answer_sealed in the answer direction with answer_iv_hex. Every body and answer carries v, the wire version, as its first member; a body whose v is absent or not version is unknown_version after it is opened and before its op is read, and an answer without it, or at another, is a lost answer. refusals are the plain answers each call may be given instead, with why. pre_body_refusals are headers a listener refuses before it reads a body, at now, for the member at standing, each answered at status with the refusal error names, in the order Prima.WorkerAuth documents: a version token other than v1, a header that does not parse, a timestamp outside window_ms, a MAC that is not the call key's, another generation, another member at the same generation, and a nonce the storage call (never retried) already presented for its attempt within the window. body_refusals are opened bodies posted at the renew route, refused with error. report is a worker service's runner_exited, plain under its dispatch key, answered plain; its cross_member names another member than the verifying one and is refused with error. retry_identity is one admit_child body sent twice, each time sealed and signed afresh under a new timestamp and nonce: the body, and so its child_key, is the same. egress_pin_cases are egress_pin calls by name, answered with a Prima.PinnedTarget (id, ip, family, scheme, port, host, expires_at) or refused as Prima.PinnedTarget.refusals/0 names; a redirect names the pin its hop came from as from. egress_policy_cases are egress_pin calls in the order one attempt makes them, under an authority whose egress.domains is domains, each answered as an egress_pin case is; expect names whether the URL's host matches domains (domain_allowed, Prima.Network.domain_allowed?/2) and, for a redirect, whether its URL has the origin of the URL whose pin it names as from (same_origin, Prima.Network.same_origin?/2: scheme, host and effective port). A pin is answered only where both hold; a first request outside domains is denied and a hop to another origin is redirect_credentials. headers_before are a hop's request headers as [name, value] pairs, and headers_after are what a hop to another origin keeps of them (Prima.Network.strip_credentials/1).
